stranded.title: The claim nobody finished
stranded.caption: Thursday. The claim lives in the table, but the memory of why lives in a process the deploy ended. Nobody asks about 4471 again, and the bank never hears a thing.

stuttering.title: The desk that just stops
stuttering.caption: After Send(B), every step is a stuttering step: each card is the one before it again. Mark(B) is allowed in every one of those states, and it never happens.

safety-liveness.title: Two kinds of promises
safety-liveness.caption: A safety violation has a moment: the strip ends at the bad card. A liveness violation has none: every card is fine, and only the strip going on forever without the good thing is wrong.

lasso.title: A path into a loop
lasso.caption: A lasso: a path from the start into a loop the behavior repeats forever. On the payout desk the loop is one state stuttering; with real cycles, TLC names the state the loop goes back to.

enabled.title: Enabled is not taken
enabled.caption: Enabled means a step of the action could be taken from this state. A behavior takes at most one step next; the other enabled steps stay enabled, not taken.

fairness.title: Weak fairness forbids waiting forever
fairness.caption: Weak fairness forbids the top line: an action enabled from some point on, forever, must eventually happen. After the crash nothing is enabled, so weak fairness makes no demand at all.

eventually-always.title: Eventually always, always eventually
eventually-always.caption: The top strip also satisfies the bottom one; not the other way round.

weak-strong.title: Weak and strong fairness
weak-strong.caption: Weak fairness only promises an action that stays enabled. Strong fairness also promises one that keeps coming back. The payout desk only needs the weak kind.

quiet-twin.title: Thursday and its quiet twin
quiet-twin.caption: The twins differ only in where the crash lands: before Send or after it. One is loud and one is quiet, and both leave a claim nobody will finish.

lease-race.title: The lease expired under a slow worker
lease-race.caption: The steps of the TLC counterexample: Claim(A), Expire, Send(A), Claim(B), Send(B). An expired lease lets someone else in; it does not stop the old holder.

resend.title: Resume sends twice
resend.caption: The steps of the TLC counterexample: Claim(A), Send(A), Crash(A), Resume(A), Send(A). The restarted worker does what a claim tells it to do: send.

idempotency-key.title: The bank remembers the key
idempotency-key.caption: The same steps as the resend: Claim(A), Send(A), Crash(A), Resume(A), Send(A). The second Send lands on a key the bank already has, so it moves no money.
